data.gender_notes: Urbanus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'urbanos', meaning 'of or pertaining to the city'. In ancient Rome, 'Urbanus' was a common name for freed slaves who had left rural life and became citizens of urban areas. The name Urbanus carries the meaning “City dweller” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Urbanus usually hope their child will grow to embody city dweller and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual journey from rural simplicity to urban complexity.
data.etymology: Urbanus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “City dweller.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Urbanus total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Οὐρβανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Οὐρβανός είναι ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη URBANUS. Η λέξη συνδέεται με την αρχαία ελληνική λέξη οὐρβανός, που σημαίνει «πόλεμος» ή «πολεμικός». Στη Νέα Κλήτευση, το όνομα εμφανίζεται ως «Οὐρβανός» και αναφέρεται σε ένα από τα μέλη της εκκλησίας της Ρώμης.

in_latin.name: Urbanus
in_latin.long_meaning: Urbanus est nomen Latinum, quod ortus est a vocabulo Urbanus, significans 'urbis' vel 'civitatis'. In Novo Testamento, nomen Urbanus apparens est, ut in Actus Apostolorum 13:1-3, ubi Urbanus est unus ex septem diaconis, qui eleguntur ab apostolis.

in_english.name: Urbanus
in_english.meaning: Derived from Latin term for urban or city
in_english.long_meaning: The name Urbanus is derived from the Latin term for urban or city. In Christian tradition, the name has historical significance as it was mentioned in the New Testament. Urbanus is one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles in the Acts of the Apostles. The name is associated with the qualities of being civic-minded, community-focused, and socially responsible. In modern times, the name Urbanus is used across various Christian cultures to represent a connection to urban communities and the values of social justice.

pronunciation.biblical: In biblical Hebrew context, no direct reference, but in Greek pronunciation: oo-rbah-NOH-s

data.cultural_impact: In the Christian context, the name Urbanus is associated with the early apostolic era. Saint Urbanus of Orléans is traditionally believed to have been a bishop in the city of Orléans, France, during the time when Bishop Elpidius is recorded as having converted the Frankish warrior Clovis to Christianity in 496 AD.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Urbanus reminds us of the importance of bringing the message of Christ to urban areas and the role of urban communities in the spread of the Gospel. It is a reminder of the transformative power of faith within cities and the potential for personal growth and spiritual renewal within an urban setting.
